resources.name: Insight
resources.desc: Very small debugger for real-mode DOS programs with Borland's Turbo like UI. Features an i80486 disassembler, and i8086 assembler.

resources.name: DIV Games Studio 2

resources.name: T3X

resources.name: SmallerC
resources.desc: Portable self-hosting C compiler capable of producing executables for a number of platforms, including real and protected mode DOS programs, by Alexei A. Frounze.

resources.name: Small-C Toolkit
resources.desc: A self-hosting Small-C Compiler Toolkit for DOS(8086) with: K&R C Compiler, Make, Linker, Assembler. First released in 1982 by Jim E. Hendrix.

resources.name: 386MAX
resources.desc: Memory manager for DOS PCs with 386 or higher CPUs, released by Qualitas company in 1992. Source code was released in June 2022 on GitHub with GPL-3.0 license.

resources.name: DOjS
resources.desc: JavaScript programming environment for MS-DOS, FreeDOS or any DOS-based Windows (like 95, 98, ME).

resources.name: The Life of MS-DOS by Brendan Byers
resources.desc: History of the DOS family including CP/M, Q-DOS/86-DOS, MS-DOS and PC-DOS. Article also includes a diagram of the timeline and family tree of DOS

resources.name: 80x86 16-bit Compiling How-to by Alexei A. Frounze
resources.desc: 16-bit compilation tutorial for Borland/Turbo C/C++ and Open Watcom. Goes into depth of memory addressing and memory models.

resources.name: 32bit DOS development with Open Watcom
resources.desc: 32-bit compilation tutorial for Open Watcom.

resources.name: How to build DOS COM files with GCC by Chris Wellons
resources.desc: Build process of Chris Wellons's DOS Defender game using DJGPP. Goal was to create a 32-bit 80386 COM executable.

resources.name: David Brackeen - 256-Color VGA Programming in C
resources.desc: Tutorial series to learn how to create graphics on DOS, written in 1996.

resources.name: 640k Really is Enough for Anyone by Robert W. Oliver II
resources.desc: Short article about getting Turbo C running on FreeDOS and moving a pixel around.

resources.name: Just keeping it real... old skool style - Scali's OpenBlog
resources.desc: Blog post about Scali's journey of doing CGA, EGA and VGA programming.

resources.name: Alex Russell's Dos Game Programming in C for Beginners
resources.desc: DOS game programming tutorial series including a primer on C, graphics, animation, input handling and collision detection. This series contains a tutorial for making buffered input handling. Last chapter contains full source code of a Break Out game on DOS.

resources.name: The Artevida Game Programming Tutorials
resources.desc: Kevin Matz's almost book-length treatment of DOS system programming and VGA programming fundamentals using C/C++ and 80x86 assembly. Unfortunately it is incomplete and was abandoned since 2001.

resources.name: PC Game Programmer's Encyclopedia
resources.desc: Collection of guides covering assembly, sound (Sound Blaster, Gravis UltraSound, PC Speaker, GameBlaster, Adlib), input, memory (EMS, XMS, DMA Transfers), PIT, VGA, SVGA, algorithms and file formats.

resources.name: The Art of Demomaking by flipcode
resources.desc: Series from 1999 that introduces to graphics programming under DOS. The home site contains other late 90s/early 2000s game programming articles as well.

resources.name: Programming MS-DOS with Power - DOS Programming, Undocumented DOS, and DOS Secrets
resources.desc: System programming tutorials like disk handling, interrupts, inputs, sound, graphics.

resources.name: Programmer's Heaven (InfoMagic)(March 1997) CD-ROM
resources.desc: Source code and files for the following topics: MS-DOS, networking, C, C++, Pascal, Visual Basic, Delphi, 3D, PC speaker, Soundblaster, Gravis Ultrasound, MIDI and many more.

resources.name: bios.h header documentation by Digital Mars
resources.desc: API documentation for routines accessing BIOS operations directly (disk operations, BIOS keyboard, printer, time, memory, serial, interrupts).

resources.name: Ralph Brown's Interrupt List - HTML version
resources.desc: List of every documented and undocumented interrupt call known, accessible through search, categories and interrupt numbers.

resources.name: A look back at memory models in 16-bit MS-DOS
resources.desc: Raymond Chen's explanation of segmented memory, including near- and far pointers.

resources.name: Values for standard video mode
resources.desc: List of all known video modes including BIOS interrupt numbers, text/pixel resolution, number of colors and video memory addresses.

resources.name: Color Graphics Adapter: Notes
resources.desc: Document describing the hardware, memory map, register I/O and hardware clones of the IBM's original CGA.

resources.name: VGA Hardware - OSDev wiki
resources.desc: Hardware guide for VGA cards that is also relevant for modern graphics cards including NVidia and ATI.

resources.name: Graphical programming in Assembly (DOS)
resources.desc: A VGA programming tutorial that also shows the list of video modes (text, CGA, EGA, VGA, SVGA) in a table at the beginning.

resources.name: VGA programming lessons
resources.desc: VGA programming tutorial series in Pascal and Assembly.

resources.name: DOS Super VGA / VESA programming notes - by Myles
resources.desc: VESA article with history at the beginning and short mention of the VESA VBE standard, but unfortunately the example codes aren't even available through Wayback Machine.

resources.name: VESA Video Modes - OSDev wiki
resources.desc: Tutorial about querying VESA modes.

resources.name: DJGPP VESA guide
resources.desc: Tutorial about querying VESA modes.

resources.name: High-res high-speed VESA tutorial
resources.desc: Series of tutorials that include drawing pixels in VESA mode (protected or real).

resources.name: C code sample for drawing in VESA 2.0 mode
resources.desc: Just code listing for drawing an ellipse in VESA mode.

resources.name: Programming Sound Cards CD
resources.desc: A 1995 CD-ROM containing source code for Adlib, Gravis, Pro-Audio, Roland and Sound Blaster sound cards. The description for the folders on the CD-ROM is listed on the back of the CD-ROM case.

resources.name: Making some noise with the PC speaker! - by Mark Feldman
resources.desc: Very short tutorial on using the PIT for generating PC speaker frequency.

resources.name: Frequencies of Musical Notes
resources.desc: Frequency table usable to parameterize the PC speaker.

resources.name: Sound Programming with PC Speaker - Chapter 23 of A to Z of C
resources.desc: PC speaker programming chapter of the "A to Z of C" book with source code.

resources.name: Yamaha YM3812 (OPL2) sound chip Wikipedia article
resources.desc: Best starting point to learn about the OPL2 sound chip besides 8-bit guy's YouTube video.

resources.name: The Ad Lib Music Synthesizer Card Programming Guide - by Tero Töttö
resources.desc: Reference of OPL2 operations and registers.

resources.name: Programmer's Guide to the Yamaha YMF 262/OPL3 FM Music Synthesizer
resources.desc: Reverse-engineered reference on OPL3.

resources.name: Sound Blaster 16 Programming Document 3.5 by Ethan Brodsky
resources.desc: Programming the Sound Blaster 16 DSP CT1341 chip for recording and playback of digitized audio.

resources.name: Soundblaster Programming Information v0.90
resources.desc: List of Sound Blaster models and registers.

resources.name: Table of DOSBox cyclecounts according to processor types
resources.desc: A table for setting the appropriate DOSBox cycle count according to CPU types (IBM XT 88, 286, 386, 486, Pentium I, Pentium II). Comes handy when you are developing a DOS game and want to simulate the environment where you intend to execute it.

resources.name: Game Engine Black Book: Wolfenstein 3D - by Fabien Sanglard
resources.desc: Fabien Sanglard's walkthrough on the game engine architecture of id Software's Wolfenstein 3D on the IBM PC's hardware. Contains forewords by John Carmack, Tom Hall and John Romero.

resources.name: Game Engine Black Book: Doom - by Fabien Sanglard
resources.desc: Fabien Sanglard's walkthrough on the game engine architecture of id Software's original Doom on Intel 486 system and game console ports. Contains forewords by John Carmack, Dave Taylor and John Romero.

resources.name: A to Z of C - a book on C/DOS programming by K. Joseph Wesley and R. Rajesh Jeba Anbiah
resources.desc: Non-profit book on programming in C on DOS. DOS system programming starts from Part II.

resources.name: Michael Abrash's Graphics Programming Black Book Special Edition
resources.desc: Collection of Michael Abrash's Dr. Dobb's Journal graphics programming articles and his work on the graphics subsystem of Quake (mirror).

resources.name: Tricks of the Game-Programming Gurus - by Andre Lamothe, John Ratcliff and Denise Tyler
resources.desc: Comprehensive DOS game development book about starting out. Topics include keyboard, mouse- and joystick input handling, creating 2D and 3D VGA graphics, raycaster rendering, sound and music, game algorithms, Interrupt Service Routines (ISR), timers, artificial intelligence, networked multiplayer through serial port and null-modem cable, tooling, parallax scrolling and optimization techniques.

resources.name: More Tricks of the Game Programming Gurus - by Greg Anderson
resources.desc: Companion book to _Tricks of the Game Programming Gurus_, continuing where the original left off. Topics include SVGA, Binary Space Partition (BSP), UI, voxel graphics, memory management in real and protected mode, advanced sound programming, debugging and optimization techniques.

resources.name: Why DOS Was (and Is) a Thing - FreeDOS
resources.desc: Historical talk starting from Unix, going through CPM, DOS 1.x, DOS 2.x, DOS 3.x, DOS 4.x, DOS 6.x, Windows 3.1, Windows 95 and ending with FreeDOS.

resources.name: CGA Graphics - Not as bad as you thought! - by 8-bit Guy
resources.desc: History and technical details about IBM's CGA system. Also describes 4-color RGBI and 16-color Composite modes.

resources.name: How Oldschool Sound/Music worked - by 8-bit Guy
resources.desc: Video about PC speaker, FM synthesizers in NES and Commodore 64, Yamaha OPL chip in AdLib and Sound Blaster sound cards, PCM samples and MOD music.

resources.name: Let's Code - MS DOS - by root42
resources.desc: DOS programming tutorial series including VGA, SoundBlaster and VGA Mode X.

resources.name: LGR - Evolution of PC Audio - As Told by Secret of Monkey Island
resources.desc: Comparison of playing the intro theme of Secret of Monkey Island through PC speaker, IBM PCjr/Tandy, AdLib, Game Blaster, Roland LAPC-1/MT-32, Gravis Ultrasound, Roland SCC-1 MIDI, SB16 Waveblaster/AWE32 and CD quality digital audio.

resources.name: Porting Retro City Rampage to MS-DOS: From PS4 to 1.44MB Floppy
resources.desc: GDC talk. Brian Provinciano's presentation on porting Retro City Rampage from PlayStation 4 to DOS. Topics include optimization, using interrupts, timing, PC speaker sound, joystick, memory management and fixed-point math.

resources.name: DOS Executables Explained - Nostalgia Nerd
resources.desc: Video about DOS executable formats including .COM, .BAT and .EXE.

resources.name: Why does DOS use 8.3 Filenames? - Nostalgia Nerd
resources.desc: Video about the 8.3 limitation of filenames under DOS, FAT partitioning scheme, NTFS, VFAT, FatGo, and LFN.EXE.

resources.name: What is DOS Protected Mode? / DOS Extenders- Nostalgia Nerd
resources.desc: Video about how PC memory looks like, conventional memory, extender memory and reasons for the need of DOS Protected Mode Interface (DPMI) and extenders like DOS/4GW.

resources.name: MS-DOS has been Open-Sourced! We Build and Run it! - Dave's Garage
resources.desc: Former Microsoft employee David Plummer tells stories about development of MS-DOS and compiles MS-DOS 4.00 source code which has been open-sourced by Microsoft.

resources.name: MS-DOS
resources.desc: GitHub repository of the original source code for MS-DOS v1.25, v2.0 and v4.0, open-sourced by Microsoft.

resources.name: FreeDOS
resources.desc: An open source DOS-compatible operating system for playing classic DOS games, running legacy business software, or developing embedded systems. Any program that works on MS-DOS should also run on FreeDOS.

resources.name: Allegro 4.2
resources.desc: Game development library for DOS, Windows and Linux. 4.2 version supports DOS platform.

resources.name: LoveDOS
resources.desc: A framework for making 2D DOS games in Lua. API based on a subset of the LÖVE API.

resources.name: DOS-VGA-Game
resources.desc: Marco A. Marrero's DOS VGA/hardware library implemented in assembly and Turbo Pascal.

resources.name: DIGPAK sound drivers source code
resources.desc: Original source code for the DIGPAK sound drivers uploaded to GitHub by John W. Ratcliff.

resources.name: DOS Defender
resources.desc: Christopher Wellons's x86 real mode DOS Asteroids clone created as an entry for Ludum Dare #31.

resources.name: Dungeons of Noudar
resources.desc: First-person 2.5D dungeon-crawler on protected mode. Written in C++, includes software rendering, fixed point math, test coverage and sound (PC speaker, Adlib, OPL2LPT).

resources.name: Emeritus Pong
resources.desc: Pong clone for DOS, Windows and Linux. Uses PC speaker for sound on DOS.

resources.name: Floppy Bird
resources.desc: Flappy Bird clone written in 16 bit assembly. Not a DOS program, but a PC-Booter application instead (although it's also possible to build a COM executable for DOS).

resources.name: George M. Tzoumas's collection of MS-DOS games and utilities
resources.desc: Turbo Pascal with few games in C and C++. Games include Nibbles, Connect Four, Ms Pacman clone and two arcade/platform games. One of them (ra2) was written using Allegro. Utilities are all written in Turbo Pascal, these include game system routines, file and disk utilities and terminate-and-stay-resident programs (TSR).

resources.name: Gold Mine Run!
resources.desc: Platformer written in C using DJGPP.

resources.name: Gridfighter 3D
resources.desc: '80s style arcade shooter written in Quickbasic. Also the very first known DOS game that supports Oculus Rift VR headset.

resources.name: Hangman
resources.desc: A Hangman clone written in Basic. Runs on at least 80286 processors and uses EGA graphics.

resources.name: Magenta's Maze
resources.desc: 3D maze game using CGA graphics with algebra as theme.

resources.name: Mario
resources.desc: Super Mario Bros clone written in Turbo Pascal.

resources.name: NetHack
resources.desc: Descendant of the original NetHack roguelike game first released in 1987 available on multiple platforms.

resources.name: Piskworks
resources.desc: Gomoku clone written in C. Works on DOS, ZX Spectrum, ZX81, ZX80, APPLE1, AS400 and Windows.

resources.name: Plutonium Caverns
resources.desc: Overhead puzzle game written in C. Web version uses DOSBox ported to Emscripten to embed DOSBox into HTML5. However, the original executable is also downloadable and buildable with Open Watcom.

resources.name: Ptakovina
resources.desc: Tetris clone written in C. Runs on DOS, Unix/Linux, ZX Spectrum and Windows.

resources.name: sudoku86
resources.desc: Sudoku clone written in C. Runs on 8086/8088 CPU, uses CGA, MCGA or VGA graphics and uses a mouse.

resources.name: Tetris
resources.desc: A Tetris clone written in assembly.

resources.name: Towers of Hanoi
resources.desc: Tower of Hanoi puzzle game written in Turbo Pascal. Originally released in 1996.

resources.name: x86 pong
resources.desc: Text-mode Pong clone written in C. Runs as PC-Booter game and under DOS.

resources.name: zmiy
resources.desc: Text-mode Snake clone written in C. Runs on 8086 DOS.

resources.name: Cyberdogs
resources.desc: Top-down 2D shooter playing as a mercenary to earn money. Written in Turbo Pascal. Supports two player mode.

resources.name: C-Dogs
resources.desc: Sequel to the original Cyberdogs. Ronny Wester, the original creator no longer maintains the website for the original C-Dogs, but multiple ports exists, including cdogs-sdl.

resources.name: Abuse
resources.desc: Sci-fi side-scrolling platform game. Regarded as an innovative cult classic by most people. Supports SVGA mode up to 1280x1024 resolution. Written in C, the architecture includes a Lisp-scripting engine.
